message.content:
Sure! Those numbers are already a pair of latitude/longitude coordinates:

| Latitude | Longitude |
|----------|-----------|
| 37.4224764 | –122.0842499 |

If you want to look up what address (or other metadata) those coordinates map to using the Google Maps Geocoding API, you’d make a reverse‑geocoding request like this:

```
https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your actual Google Maps API key. The JSON response will contain an array of results; the first one typically gives the most relevant address. For these coordinates you’ll see something like:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      ...
    }
  ],
  "status": "OK"
}
```

So the coordinates point to the Googleplex in Mountain View, California.
